title: Wasserstein approximation of measures via orthogonal frames: statistical and computational complexities
abstract: arXiv:2610.36581v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Dimension-reduction methods such as PCA identify a subspace capturing most of the variation in the data, but not a distinguished basis within it. Selecting a basis in which the samples are sparsely represented is a recurring task in unsupervised learning, addressed by methods in factor analysis, dictionary learning, and subspace clustering. We pose this task as Wasserstein approximation of the data distribution by measures supported on the axes of an orthogonal frame, which, in turn, reduces to a nonsmooth optimization problem over the orthogonal group $\mathrm{O}(d)$. We show that, under mild assumptions, both empirical risk minimizers and a locally initialized stochastic gradient method recover the population-optimal frame at the near-parametric rate $\widetilde{O}_d(n^{-1/2})$, where $n$ is the sample size. The main difficulty is that, although the population objective is smooth, the empirical objective is not-this mismatch preclude

translated_title: 通过正交框架实现测度的Wasserstein逼近：统计与计算复杂度
translated_abstract: 诸如主成分分析（PCA）之类的降维方法能够识别出捕捉数据大部分变异的子空间，但无法确定该子空间内的一个特殊基。选择一个使样本能够被稀疏表示的基，是无监督学习中反复出现的任务，因子分析、字典学习和子空间聚类等方法都在处理这一问题。我们将此任务表述为：用支撑在某个正交框架各坐标轴上的测度对数据分布进行Wasserstein逼近，这进而归结为正交群 $\mathrm{O}(d)$ 上的一个非光滑优化问题。我们证明，在温和的假设条件下，无论是经验风险最小化方法，还是局部初始化的随机梯度方法，都能以近参数速率 $\widetilde{O}_d(n^{-1/2})$（其中 $n$ 为样本量）恢复出总体最优的正交框架。主要困难在于：尽管总体目标是光滑的，经验目标却非光滑——这种不匹配阻碍了……（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文将无监督学习中的稀疏表示基选择任务转化为用正交框架轴上测度进行Wasserstein逼近的非光滑优化问题，并证明经验风险最小化和局部初始化的随机梯度方法均能以近参数速率 n^{-1/2} 恢复总体最优的正交框架。
en_tdlr: This paper recasts basis selection for sparse representation as Wasserstein approximation of the data distribution by measures supported on orthogonal frame axes—a nonsmooth optimization problem over O(d)—and proves that both empirical risk minimizers and a locally initialized stochastic gradient method recover the population-optimal frame at the near-parametric rate n^{-1/2}.
